results.description: ManPQN and NLS-ManPG need less line-search steps than ManPG and ManPG-Ada on the CM problem.
results.evidence: File: results/formal/paper_scale/metrics.json. Only 3 of 14 required dataset configurations are present (n=128/256/512, r=4, mu=0.1); n=64, mu=0.15, r=1/2/6/8, and mu=0.05/0.20/0.25 configs are absent. For the 3 configs found, averaged line_search_steps are: (1) n=128,r=4,mu=0.1: ManPQN=519.4, NLS-ManPG=0.2, ManPG=0.0, ManPG-Ada=0.2; (2) n=256,r=4,mu=0.1: ManPQN=0.0, NLS-ManPG=42.4, ManPG=0.0, ManPG-Ada=42.4; (3) n=512,r=4,mu=0.1: ManPQN=0.0, NLS-ManPG=123.8, ManPG=0.0, ManPG-Ada=123.8. Constraint 'ManPQN > ManPG' (ManPQN strictly fewer steps) fails all 3 configs — ManPG has 0 steps while ManPQN has 519.4, 0.0, 0.0. Constraint 'NLS-ManPG > ManPG' fails all 3 — ManPG=0.0 but NLS-ManPG=0.2, 42.4, 123.8. Constraint 'NLS-ManPG > ManPG-Ada' fails all 3 — NLS-ManPG equals ManPG-Ada exactly. Only 'ManPQN > ManPG-Ada' passes 2 of 3 configs.
results.note: The run outputs are both incomplete (11 of 14 required configs missing) and contradictory to the claim: ManPG and ManPG-Ada consistently use zero or fewer line-search steps than ManPQN and NLS-ManPG in the available outputs, opposite to what the paper claims.
